overall: The AG found the Evaluation Subcommittee violated the OML when two of its three members (a quorum) deliberated on the Superintendent's performance outside a posted meeting, but found no Committee-level violation on either complaint.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged a quorum of the seven-member Committee deliberated on October 30 outside a properly posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law by deliberating outside of a properly posted meeting where the discussions on October 30 occurred between three Committee members, which is not a quorum of the Committee.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged a quorum of the three-member Evaluation Subcommittee deliberated on October 30 outside a properly posted meeting about the Superintendent.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that a quorum of the Subcommittee deliberated outside of a properly posted meeting on October 30, and therefore violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Second complainant alleged a quorum of the Committee deliberated about the Superintendent's contract between November 6 and 14 outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that a quorum of the Committee did not deliberate outside of a properly posted meeting and therefore did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements, with a caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements, and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
